data.description:
# Filter core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` out of generated game repos

**Cross-repo delivery counterpart of** `MS-0MVSBGYMD009CP7D` (tce-main-street) — _Deliver core template change to Tableau-Card-Engine (parent AC3)_ — and of `MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0` (its parent, the discovery item).

## Why this item exists

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declared
`scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` pointing at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — a file
that exists only in the core (Option C: a game repo has no root `scripts/` tree). Invoking
either script failed with module-not-found.

Root cause: `renderPackageJson` in `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherited the core's whole
`scripts` map, so the core's own `scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` entries leaked into every
generated repo.

## The change (authored, tracked here for landing on the engine's `dev`)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`: an explicitly named `CORE_ONLY_SCRIPTS` drop-list filters
  both keys out of the inherited scripts map, with the Option C rationale inline and the wider
  class of core-only scripts left to a follow-up.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`: the `MANIFEST` fixture declares both keys and a
  new test asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them while other inherited scripts
  (e.g. `save-load-smoke`) and the game-repo `scaffold` entry point still pass through.

Both land in one commit (test-first: the test asserts absence, so the engine's dev-push gate
would refuse the test without the filter).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `renderPackageJson` omits `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from the rendered game-repo
   `package.json` while every other inherited script passes through unchanged.
2. A unit test asserts the same via `renderPackageJson` against a manifest declaring both keys.
3. The change is merged to the engine's `dev` branch with the full-suite dev-push gate green.

## Notes

- The consumer-side `./core` submodule pointer bump is owned by the tce-main-street item
  `MS-0MVSB5TYD000K5N6` (blocked by `MS-0MVSBGYMD009CP7D`), not by this item.

data.description:
Cross-repo delivery counterpart of MS-0MVSB5Y83001XSU2 (tce-main-street, AC4): one-line 'run from the core checkout' invocation-context clarifications in the core docs that use the core-only scaffold commands.

## Why

The game-repo scaffold entry point is 'npm run scaffold' (drives the engine-owned generator via --core-root ./core). 'scaffold:game' and 'scaffold:games' are **core-checkout-only** npm scripts; the parent epic (MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0) filtered them out of generated game repos. The core docs still name them (legitimately, for core use), but where the invocation context could be read as a game-repo command, a one-line 'run from the core checkout' clarification is added (parent AC4).

## Scope

- docs/DEVELOPER.md — 'Scaffolding a game repo' section: the `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts ...` and `npm run scaffold:games` invocations.
- docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md — 'Repository scaffold and multi-repo setup': `npm run scaffold:game` / `npm run scaffold:games` block.
- docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md — 'Per-game repo scaffold (F4)': `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts ...` + `npm run scaffold:games`.

Only where ambiguity exists; each site is already core-checkout context, so a one-line clarification is added, not a rewrite.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the three core docs adds a one-line 'run from the core checkout' clarification at the scaffold invocation site(s) where the context could be mistaken for a game-repo command.
2. No generated game repo or consumer-path doc (game-repo-context) is affected.
3. The change lands on the engine dev branch with the dev-push gate green; the engine commit SHA is recorded on both this item and MS-0MVSB5Y83001XSU2.
